summary: Bidirectional alignment fails: grading-relevant regulated-workload identity conflicts across docs/starter vs data/verifier, apps/batch UpgradeProtected+label obligations are phantom relative to the solver-visible work request, and instruction.md is a one-to-one compressed F2P rubric.

evidence.observation: 20 Edition-3 bullets state plan/IRSA/PDB/placement/rollout/checkpoint/report obligations; system-node taints/labels only; no apps/batch UpgradeProtected obligation; no regulated workload names.
Names regulated workloads payment-authorizer and settlement-reconciler; describes system/application node groups with protection tags.
Authoritative graded workload list contains only settlement-ledger on regulated-on-demand.
Starter manifests ship payment-authorizer and settlement-reconciler, not settlement-ledger.
Incident evidence names settlement-ledger on spot after interruption; UpgradeProtected gap cited only for system node group.
Asserts UpgradeProtected=true and nodepool labels for system, apps, and batch.
Grades report['regulated_placement'] entries produced from regulated_policy workloads (settlement-ledger).
plan_policy_errors requires apps/batch UpgradeProtected; run_rollout placement loop keys regulated_policy workloads; drain_result hardcoded true after PDB presence.
Acceptance-checklist shaped restatement of plan/IRSA/PDB/READY gates overlapping instruction bullets.
irsa_bindings includes role_arn; addon-trust-rollout-contract.md omits role_arn for the same field.
Reverse-outline and hidden-test inventory prohibitions; requirements must be discoverable without one-bullet-per-test rubric topology.

findings.criterion: grading-relevant ambiguity on regulated workload identity
findings.why_it_matters: Solvers following architecture/starter names (payment-authorizer, settlement-reconciler) fail placement gates that grade settlement-ledger from regulated_policy; conflicting authorities change pass/fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Make one authoritative workload identity set consistent across architecture.md, starter k8s, evidence, regulated_policy.json, and verifier placement checks; reference that set from instruction.md.
findings.regression_risk: Low if names/selectors stay aligned with existing regulated_policy and interruption evidence.

findings.criterion: phantom verifier obligation for apps/batch UpgradeProtected and labels
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction only requires CriticalAddonsOnly taint and nodepool labels on the system node group and guarding already-tagged UpgradeProtected resources; READY still requires apps and batch UpgradeProtected plus labels via plan_policy and F2P assertions.
findings.minimal_remediation: Either state apps/batch label and UpgradeProtected preservation in the solver-visible work request/contract, or drop those assertions from plan_policy_errors and tests.
findings.regression_risk: Medium: loosening policy without documenting preservation could allow unprotected node-group replaces.

findings.why_it_matters: Twenty concise bullets track F2P cases nearly one-to-one (plan versions, PRESERVE, SSM tags, IRSA, PDBs, drain, regulated placement, Karpenter, interruption, order, readiness, cross-service, policy merge, UpgradeProtected, checkpoint, report digest), failing the reverse-outline test and leaking rubric structure.
findings.minimal_remediation: Regroup into fewer responsibility-oriented requirements while retaining every material obligation; keep detailed schema/order in legitimate docs rather than a bullet-per-test inventory.
findings.regression_risk: Medium: regrouping can accidentally omit a material obligation if not matrix-checked.

findings.criterion: vacuous/weak F2P ownership for drain simulation
findings.why_it_matters: After PDBs exist, run_rollout hardcodes pdb_respected/core_available success; the F2P drain test does not exercise agent-owned drain behavior or minAvailable enforcement beyond PDB presence already covered elsewhere, so the drain requirement is not meaningfully tested.
findings.minimal_remediation: Make drain outcomes depend on submitted PDB thresholds/replicas (or agent-reported drain artifacts) with a failing counterexample when budgets are wrong.
findings.regression_risk: Low if PDB fixtures already encode the intended budgets.

findings.criterion: material CLI entrypoint requirement not meaningfully tested
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction requires execution via /app/bin/addon-trust-rollout, but P2P only checks upgrade_lab callables and no test invokes or asserts the public CLI path.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a behavioral check that the public CLI exists and produces the graded report/plan artifacts, or narrow the instruction if CLI is non-graded.

findings.why_it_matters: role_arn presence differs between schema docs; digest omits role_arn, so impact is limited but contracts disagree.
findings.minimal_remediation: Align both docs with the digest/stable field set actually graded.

findings.why_it_matters: addon-trust-rollout-contract.md reads as a second acceptance checklist overlapping instruction goals rather than pure architecture/schema documentation.
findings.minimal_remediation: Keep end-state asks in instruction.md; leave docs to schemas, inventories, and operator procedures without rubric restatement.
